A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EchoMimicV2 and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. All supplied pages were inspected, including v4's added Section 7, Supplementary Material; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results and component ablations in Table 2, together with generated animation examples in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds qualitative denoising-stage and pose-free animation results in Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: The APDH strategy, Head Partial Attention, temporal modules, and PhD objective remain unchanged. Section 7 presents Gaussian pose maps and differentiable Canny processing as implementation details of existing losses. The pose-free variant was already described in v2.

E1.justification: Both retain HumanVid, the half-body and headshot training collections, EMTD evaluation, and FLUX-generated reference images. Pose-free animation and missing or deformed reference hands were already considered in v2; the supplementary visualizations introduce no distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains AnimateAnyone, MimicMotion, and the same ablation and straightforward-baseline rows. Figures 4–5 retain the same qualitative comparisons, including Vlogger and CyberHost. Citation renumbering does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds a diagnostic visualization protocol using one-step predictions and VAE decoding at selected denoising timesteps. Existing training and benchmark settings remain unchanged. The listed timesteps, 30/150/500/1000, do not fully agree with Figure 7's 3%/10%/50%/100% labels.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds visual evidence examining the proposed progression from pose to detail to visual quality. Figure 8 supplies examples for the pose-free analysis already described in v2 Section 4.4. The quantitative component ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Table 2 retains the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 140 numerical entries in Table 2 are identical, including EchoMimicV2's FID of 49.33 and FVD of 598.45. Figures 7–8 add qualitative result frames showing denoising progression and detailed but motion-limited hands without pose conditioning.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) and the three-phase objective remain mathematically unchanged. Section 7's differentiability discussion supplies implementation explanation, without adding a formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about simplified half-body animation, APDH, headshot augmentation, PhD Loss, the benchmark, and superiority over existing methods. The supplementary evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 refines the interpretation of hand-pose conditioning by distinguishing preserved hand appearance from restricted motion range and diversity after its removal. v2 emphasized rhythmic general gestures and inability to generate specific gestures. The phase rationale and Section 5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly specifies Gaussian maps for the pose loss and removal of nondifferentiable Canny operations through a fixed convolutional implementation. It also identifies video and dataset-URL files within a supplementary archive. These improve documentation; the archive's actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds four introductory references covering the PIRM enhancement challenge, neural architecture search, domain adaptation, and domain generalization. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against human-animation methods are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v4 adds Section 7 before the references, makes limited grammatical edits, adjusts the introductory opening, and expands the author-contribution footnote. The main narrative and ordering of Sections 1–6 remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 7–8 and their captions, adjusts abstract typesetting, and reflows text around page boundaries. Figures 1–6 and the structures of Tables 1–2 are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the denoising rationale and previously described pose-free analysis more inspectable through Figures 7–8, while clarifying backpropagation through the pose and detail losses. These provide useful, limited gains in transparency and reproducibility. The quantitative evidence remains unchanged, and the new timestep-label inconsistency limits the precision of the supplementary analysis.
